# rsync exclude rules for the production (cPanel) deployment.
#
# Single source of truth: deploy.sh uses this exact file for the self-test,
# the dry-run plan and the real upload, and refuses to run if a mandatory rule
# below is missing. Comments must be on their own line (rsync does not support
# trailing comments).
#
# Pattern syntax:
#   leading "/"   anchors the rule to the repository root
#   trailing "/"  matches directories only
#   no "/"        matches that exact name at ANY depth
#
# Excluded paths are never copied, overwritten or deleted on the server.
# (deploy.sh never uses --delete, so files that exist only on production are
# preserved as well.)

# --- 1. Production-owned: must never be copied, uploaded or overwritten -----
# Environment files that hold production credentials (any depth).
.env
.env.*
# Web-server rules, including the cPanel-generated PHP settings (any depth,
# so system/.htaccess and app/ThirdParty/tcpdf/tools/.htaccess are skipped too).
.htaccess
# Production Composer dependencies. Root only: app/Libraries/vendor is real
# application code and must keep deploying.
/vendor/
# Production public assets and uploads.
/public/
# Runtime data: per-company files, cache, logs, sessions.
/writable/

# --- 2. Additional protective excludes (not on the owner's original list) ---
# Server-level PHP settings written by cPanel's MultiPHP INI editor; a stale
# repo copy must not overwrite what is configured on the server.
/.user.ini
/php.ini
# Repository and CI internals must never land in a web-served directory.
.git
/.github/
